row.evidence: No, Zendesk does not currently support any official SCIM connections; Okta and Entra have built integrations that connect directly to Zendesk API endpoints to achieve some of the functionality that SCIM provides.
row.notes: Status changed from partial (June) to none under the post-pilot rule for provisioning without SCIM: Zendesk's help centre says it does not support any official SCIM connections, and Okta, Microsoft Entra and Google Workspace provision Zendesk through IdP-built connectors that call Zendesk's own REST API (Users, Groups, Group Memberships), so row.api_provisioning is true and those IdPs are api_connector. The June row's 'SCIM 2.0 (via Okta/Entra)' wording is corrected: the connectors are not SCIM. Plan gate: Zendesk publishes none for this API-based provisioning (API access is shown on the pricing page without a tier restriction). The only gate found, 'Professional plan or better', comes from Microsoft's Entra provisioning tutorial, not from a Zendesk page, and Okta's docs state no plan requirement; the pilot's 'Suite Professional' SCIM plan rested on that Microsoft page and is dropped from scim_plan. SAML SSO (with JIT, also for JWT and OIDC) is on every plan including Support Team. Audit log API is Enterprise only. Pricing changed since June: Suite Team is now $55/agent/mo annual ($69 monthly), Suite Professional $115 annual ($149 monthly); the cheapest paid tier is Support Team at $19. Zendesk now marks API tokens (used by the Okta and Entra connectors) as deprecated in favour of OAuth.

limitations.text: No native SCIM endpoint on any plan. Okta and Microsoft Entra integrations call Zendesk's own REST API endpoints instead and replicate some SCIM functionality, including custom user field mapping.

rate_limits.text: Support and Help Center API requests per minute by Suite plan: Team 200, Growth 400, Professional 400, Enterprise 700, Enterprise Plus 2500; 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. High Volume API add-on (2500 rpm) on Suite Growth+ / Support Professional+, minimum 10 agent seats.

limitations.text: Custom agent roles (and assigning them via custom_role_id) require the Enterprise plan or above.
Audit Logs endpoints are Enterprise only.
API tokens and basic authentication are being retired; existing customers must migrate to OAuth access tokens.

google.notes: Zendesk has no SCIM endpoint, so Google's Zendesk auto-provisioning must use Zendesk's own API; Google's page does not say who built the connector.

fallbacks.other_sync: No directory/HRIS sync documented by Zendesk; provisioning from Okta, Microsoft Entra and Google Workspace runs through IdP-built connectors on the Zendesk REST API.

open_questions: Zendesk does not publish a plan requirement for Okta/Entra/Google API-based provisioning; Microsoft's Entra tutorial says 'Professional plan or better' while Okta states none. Which Zendesk plans actually support the IdP connectors (Support Team, Suite Team)?
Microsoft's 'Professional plan' wording may refer to Support Professional (no longer on the public pricing page) or Suite Professional; unclear which.

Zendesk docs do not say what IdP-driven deprovisioning does to the agent seat (Okta says it deactivates or suspends the user); whether suspending or downgrading frees a paid agent seat is not documented in the pages loaded.
Whether suspension revokes active sessions is not stated on the Users API page (POST /api/v2/users/logout_many exists separately).
OneLogin's Zendesk connector page returned an HTTP 202 bot challenge to curl and an empty page in a headless browser, so OneLogin SSO/provisioning support could not be verified.
JumpCloud's Zendesk article documents SAML SSO with JIT provisioning only; it neither confirms nor rules out SCIM/API provisioning, so provisioning is left null.
Suite Enterprise and Enterprise Plus prices are not published (Talk to Sales); the Enterprise column is not in the public comparison table.
